ai.description: *Megophrys zhangi* is a medium-sized toad (45–60 mm) with brown dorsal skin and dark lateral patches. It features prominent horn-like skin projections above the eyes and a distinct, triangular head.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys zhangi* is best distinguished by its distinct, elongated, triangular dermal horn above each eye, which is significantly more prominent than in other Indian species.
ai.habitat: Zhang's Horned Toad inhabits humid subtropical evergreen forests and mountain streams at altitudes ranging from 1,800 to 2,800 meters in the Eastern Himalayas.
ai.behavior: Zhang's Horned Toad is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among leaf litter during the day to ambush passing insects with its highly effective sit-and-wait strategy.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys zhangi* breeds in streams during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of pigmented eggs attached to the undersides of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: Megophrys zhangi is found in the high-altitude regions of Arunachal Pradesh, India, typically inhabiting elevations between 2,000 and 3,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The call of *Megophrys zhangi* consists of a series of short, low-pitched, metallic "cluck" notes, typically heard echoing near mountain streams in its forest habitat.
